# The effects syntax

<!-- Generated by tools/quality/genGrammar.ts from packages/core/src/grammar.ts and plan.ts. Do not edit: a test fails when this file differs from its generator, and parses every example below. -->

One story is one `.fountain` file. Dialogue is prose, byte for byte what is spoken and subtitled; every Element and every effect is written once, with its id, in the Scene it belongs to (spec 0002). Nothing is positional: no `next`, no "the Element above", no bare flag.

## A Scene, in one view

**Two Scenes: a sound on the move, a reveal after a word, a focus before one**

```fountain
Title: Same name, new place

# Two screens

INT. THE FIRST SCREEN - DAY #sc3#

Box one {id=one cell=ml class=box}
Every box has a name {id=tag cell=tc class=label}

NARRATOR
A box on the first screen.

> AUTO-ANIMATE

INT. THE NEXT SCREEN - DAY #sc4#

Box one {id=one cell=mc class=box}
Every box has a name {id=tag cell=tc class=accent}
Same name, so it moves {id=hint cell=bc class=muted}
Matched by id {id=note cell=br class=label visible=false}

[[effects
  s1: sound whoosh at one.move.start
  s2: sound ding   at one.move.50%
  r1: show  note   at word("matches").end +0.1s
  f1: focus hint   at word("slides").start -0.2s
]]

NARRATOR
On the next screen, box one sits somewhere else. Its name matches, so it slides there.
```

**One Scene: the slide change, the second of three words, an absolute time with its reason, a chain**

```fountain
Title: Example

# Part

INT. THE ONLY SCREEN - DAY #only#

A title {id=title cell=mc class=title}

[[effects
  w1: sound whoosh at transition.start
  w2: sound ding at word("again", 2).end
  w3: sound pop at 2.5s because "the music has a beat here"
  w4: sound pop at w1.end +3f
]]

NARRATOR
Say it, and say it again. Then say it again.
```

## The Scene heading

The id sits between `#` at the end of the heading: `INT. THE NEXT SCREEN - DAY #sc4#`. It is required, unique in the story, and starts with a letter followed by letters, digits, `_` or `-`; `scene`, `transition`, `word` are reserved by the anchor grammar (no Scene, Element or effect may carry one).

## Element lines

One Action line is one Element: its text, then `{key=value ...}`. Every property is named; there are no sigils and no bare flags.

| key | required | default | values | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | yes |  | an identifier: a letter, then letters, digits, `_` and `-` | names the Element; unique in its Scene; the identity diff matches Elements by it |
| `cell` | yes |  | `tl`, `tc`, `tr`, `ml`, `mc`, `mr`, `bl`, `bc`, `br` | where the Element sits on the 3 x 3 grid, in reading order |
| `class` | yes |  | `box`, `title`, `label`, `accent`, `muted` | how the fixed theme draws it (one class) |
| `visible` | no | `true` | `true`, `false` | `false`: the Element starts hidden and exactly one `show` effect reveals it |

Cells: `tl`, `tc`, `tr`, `ml`, `mc`, `mr`, `bl`, `bc`, `br`. Classes: `box`, `title`, `label`, `accent`, `muted`.

## The effects block

One `[[effects` block per Scene, before its first dialogue, with no blank line inside. Each line is one effect: its id, a verb with its argument, and when it happens.

```text
block    ::= "[[effects" NEWLINE { line NEWLINE } "]]"
line     ::= id ":" verb argument "at" when
verb     ::= "sound" sound name (pop, whoosh, ding) | "show" element id | "focus" element id
when     ::= anchor [ offset ] | absolute
absolute ::= number "s" "because" quoted
anchor   ::= <effect>.start|end | <element>.enter|exit|move|update.start|end|<N>% | scene.start|end | transition.start|end|<N>% | word("<phrase>"[, <n>]).start|end
edge     ::= "start" | "end"
event    ::= "enter" | "exit" | "move" | "update"
offset   ::= ( "+" | "-" ) number ( "ms" | "s" | "f" | "%" )
id       ::= letter { letter | digit | "_" | "-" }
```

### Verbs

| verb | argument | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sound` | sound name (pop, whoosh, ding) | plays a sound of the built-in catalogue |
| `show` | element id | reveals an Element that is `visible=false` |
| `focus` | element id | rings and scales an Element of this Scene |

### Anchors

An anchor names a moment of the Plan. It resolves to a frame in the schedule stage, from the aligned words and the renderer's declared lifecycle; `reebeat plan` prints `intent -> frame` for each effect.

| anchor | points at |
| --- | --- |
| `<effect>.start\|end` | another effect of this Scene: its own start (its fire frame) or end (a show: its fire frame plus the renderer's show time; a sound or focus: its fire frame) |
| `<element>.enter\|exit\|move\|update.start\|end\|<N>%` | a lifecycle event of an Element of this Scene (exit: of the previous Scene, seen at the transition): the first frame it differs, the frame it settles, or N percent of the way (move and update: by the renderer's declared easing) |
| `scene.start\|end` | scene.start: the frame the slide change is shown; scene.end: the last frame of the Scene |
| `transition.start\|end\|<N>%` | the Scene's incoming slide transition: its first frame, its last frame, or N percent of the way (linear in time) |
| `word("<phrase>"[, <n>]).start\|end` | a word or phrase of this Scene's narration: the start of its first word or the end of its last; n picks the nth occurrence and is required when the phrase occurs more than once |

Edges: `start`, `end`. Element events: `enter`, `exit`, `move`, `update`. A percent is only valid on an anchor that has a window (a move, an update, a show, the transition of a Scene that is not `> CUT`, a word); an instant (an exit, `scene.start`, a sound) has none.

### Offsets

After an anchor: a sign, a number and a unit.

| unit | means |
| --- | --- |
| `ms` | milliseconds |
| `s` | milliseconds, written in seconds (x 1000) |
| `f` | frames |
| `%` | a share of the anchored window (only with an anchor that has one) |

### Absolute times

An effect may be pinned to a time from the slide change, `at 2.5s because "<reason>"`. The reason is mandatory; `reebeat lint` and `reebeat plan` list every absolute time.

### Sounds

The catalogue: `pop`, `whoosh`, `ding`.

## What is rejected, and what the message says

Each form below is an error that names its line, what was found, what was expected and the nearest valid form.

**A Scene heading without its id**

```fountain-invalid
Title: Example

# Part

INT. THE ONLY SCREEN - DAY

A title {id=title cell=mc class=title}

NARRATOR
Hello.
```

> line 5, BadSceneId: Scene heading "INT. THE ONLY SCREEN - DAY" has no id; expected the id between # at the end of the heading, as "INT. THE NEXT SCREEN - DAY #sc4#"; did you mean "INT. THE ONLY SCREEN - DAY #sc1#"?

**An Element in the release-1 form**

```fountain-invalid
Title: Example

# Part

INT. THE ONLY SCREEN - DAY #only#

A title {#title @mc .title hidden}

NARRATOR
Hello.
```

> line 7, ReleaseOneForm: release-1 Element form {#title @mc .title hidden}; expected key=value properties: A title {id=title cell=mc class=title visible=false}

**A note in dialogue (release 1)**

```fountain-invalid
Title: Example

# Part

INT. THE ONLY SCREEN - DAY #only#

A title {id=title cell=mc class=title}

NARRATOR
Hello [[next]] there.
```

> line 10, ReleaseOneForm: release-1 cue [[next]] in dialogue; expected no note in dialogue; write r1: show <element id> at word("Hello").end in the [[effects]] block of the Scene

**An unknown event, with the nearest valid one**

```fountain-invalid
Title: Example

# Part

INT. THE ONLY SCREEN - DAY #only#

A title {id=title cell=mc class=title}
A hint {id=hint cell=bc class=muted visible=false}

[[effects
  r1: show hint at word("hello").end
  s1: sound pop at hint.entr.start
]]

NARRATOR
Hello there.
```

> line 12, BadEffect: unknown event "entr" in hint.entr.start; expected enter, exit, move or update; did you mean enter?

**A phrase that occurs twice, with no occurrence number**

```fountain-invalid
Title: Example

# Part

INT. THE ONLY SCREEN - DAY #only#

A title {id=title cell=mc class=title}

[[effects
  s1: sound pop at word("again").end
]]

NARRATOR
Again and again.
```

> line 10, AmbiguousWord: word("again") occurs 2 times in Scene only; expected the occurrence you mean; did you mean word("again", 1) to word("again", 2)?

**An absolute time without its reason**

```fountain-invalid
Title: Example

# Part

INT. THE ONLY SCREEN - DAY #only#

A title {id=title cell=mc class=title}

[[effects
  s1: sound pop at 2.5s
]]

NARRATOR
Hello.
```

> line 10, AbsoluteNeedsReason: absolute time "2.5s" has no reason; expected at 2.5s because "<why this moment is fixed>"

### The release-1 forms

| release 1 | now |
| --- | --- |
| `[[next]]` in dialogue | a `show` line in the `[[effects]]` block: `r1: show <element id> at word("<phrase>").end`, and `visible=false` on the Element |
| `[[focus: id]]` in dialogue | a `focus` line in the `[[effects]]` block: `f1: focus <element id> at word("<phrase>").end` |
| `[[sfx: name]]` in dialogue | a `sound` line in the `[[effects]]` block: `s1: sound <name> at word("<phrase>").end`, or `at transition.start` for the slide change |
| `{#id @cell .class hidden}` | `{id=<id> cell=<cell> class=<class> visible=false}` |
| a Scene heading without `#id#` | `INT. THE NEXT SCREEN - DAY #sc4#` |
